dedupe_keys.name: public transport accessibility levels ptal 2023 grid greater london

description: The PTAL 2023 grid measures access to public transport across Greater London on a 100 m by 100 m grid. For each grid centroid, walk times along an Ordnance Survey walk network are computed to nearby stops and stations within set limits (for example 8 minutes to bus stops and 12 minutes to rail stations), average waiting times are derived from service frequencies in TfL's RailPlan 8.3 scenario, and total access times with mode reliability factors are turned into access index values. The dataset includes separate access indices for bus, London Underground, rail and tram, a total access index and the PTAL class from 0 (very poor) to 6b (excellent). Coverage is Greater London. Access: free CSV and ArcGIS feature service under the Open Government Licence v3.0, containing OS data; the items were last modified in July 2026. Caveats: PTAL measures service density near a place, not travel times to destinations, and a development copy of the layer carries TfL WebCAT terms instead. It supports public transport accessibility and equity analysis, exposure of transit-dependent areas to service disruption and planning of service changes, and complements the TfL Unified API and the SEDAC SDG 11.2.1 indicator catalogued here.
